Progression

Material Realms and relics

One tool per swing, a reward per point of durability, and every reward multiplied by your promotion's factor. Pick a material below for its table by promotion; the Relics tab prices every level in the sand you actually mine. For what those swings are worth in season points, use the Primostar planner.

1 toolper swing, no free swings
≈ 11durability per swing: 10 × 0.9–1.1, 20% crit ×1.5
×10 → ×10.8Champion I to Champion II: +8% on every reward
25 : 5 : 1Chrono Sand per Epic Chrono Sand and Rare Chrono Sand

The rule card in the game: "Use specific items in mines/caves to gather ores and defeat monsters for rewards." "The rankings will track the number of ores mined and monsters defeated." Reward counts are reward_rule base × level_number column 6 at your sub-rank, rounded down; the realm "level" only tracks which unlock fights you have cleared and scales nothing. Quick mode swings until the object breaks (64 per request) once Loong Haven is open. Per-swing figures are averages over the swing roll.

Dustfall Dune, one Sand Shovel per swing. What the realm puts in front of you: Chrono Sand Mine (80%, 90 durability, about 9 swings); Moment Sand Mine (15%, 90 durability, about 9 swings); Abandoned Ore Chest: Chrono Sand (5%, opens free).

Sand grades. 5 Chrono Sand = 1 Rare Chrono Sand → 5 Rare Chrono Sand = 1 Epic Chrono Sand, so 1 Epic Chrono Sand is 25 Chrono Sand; the game merges upward for you when a cost asks for a grade you lack (item_merge, CalcMergeCost). The next two grades have no active recipe in this build.

A relic has normal levels up to a cap set by your promotion (+1 per tier: Expert III 10, Champion III 13, Master III 16). Past the cap the level is a season level ("Levels beyond your Rank's cap are calculated as Season Levels."): sold only at the top tier of the season's promotion, priced from that promotion's ladder, and gone when the season ends. So the same number costs different things in different seasons — level 10 → 11: in Season 1 it is season level 1, sold at Expert III only: 3,200 Rare Chrono Sand (16,000 Chrono Sand) and 28,800 Rolla; from Season 2 to 5 it is normal level 11, open from Champion I: 900 Epic Chrono Sand (22,500 Chrono Sand) and 40,500 Rolla.

Where this comes from

Realms: mop_up_dungeon (tools, unlock fights, object pools), mop_up_material (durability, per-point and break reward rules), reward_rule scaled by level_number as RewardRuleInfoParser.GetRewardDropInfosByRuleList does it, level_prop for the swing stats, BattleFormulaHandler.GetMopUpDamage for the roll, game_settings.MopUp, rule_tip, stage and stage_map_location; sand grades from item_merge. Relics: treasure_levelup_material, treasure_bless, treasure_upgrade_material, system_level_limit, system_level_gap_limit, read the way TreasureHelper reads them; seasons from astrological_season_config. Names are the game's English strings. One assumption: the server pays the per-point reward per point of durability removed; the client never computes it, so a swing that overkills an object may pay for the whole roll or only for the durability left.

Purrwikimania — an independent, fan-made reference for Sword x Staff (Boltray Games). Every number here is read directly out of the game's own configuration files and decompiled code, not from testing or estimation. Item names are the game's official English strings.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Boltray Games. Game names, images and data are the property of their owners. Figures reflect the client build they were extracted from and can change with any patch — see Method for exactly what was read and when.
